bearings.paper_claim: SMOreg trained on EAR observer ratings (96 speakers, 10-fold CV) has relative absolute error above the mean baseline for all five traits: E 140.05, ES 162.05, A 173.97, C 131.75, O 213.20 percent (baseline 100). The authors say linear regression and SVMs perform poorly and suggest they need a bigger dataset.
bearings.paper_location: Table 19 p.482 (Sec 5.2 starts p.481); Ramey et al. 2016 footnote 4 (text line 122)
bearings.system_side: fit_smoreg_rkh.py takes Ramey per-member trait averages as targets. big5_traits.py loads liwc/mairesse_smoreg.json as ACTIVE weights when the file exists, replacing the published-correlate weights.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds as a statement about the Mairesse observer model and Ramey fn 4. The paper never says what data the distributed observer model was fit on, so the claim that it was fit on all 96 speakers is an assumption. Ramey line 191 calls the training sample the essay sample, so Ramey is internally inconsistent on provenance.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and Ramey fn 4 verified. Softened: the all-96 fit claim is not in the paper. The claim that the active JSON now holds the RKH refit is unverified: fit_smoreg_rkh.py writes liwc/rkh_calibrated.json.candidate (line 89-90), that file is absent from the repo, and the essays script writes mairesse_smoreg.json.candidate. No code path read promotes RKH weights into the active file.

bearings.paper_claim: On the essays corpus with self-reports, SMO binary accuracy is 54.9 to 62.1 percent (openness 62.1 vs 50.3 baseline). SMOreg relative error is E 100.65, ES 98.35, A 100.28, C 99.30 (none significant) and O 94.19 (significant). Best Pearson r is 0.33 for openness and 0.24 for emotional stability.
bearings.paper_location: Table 12 p.475; Table 17 p.481 (Sec 5.1 p.480); Pearson r in Sec 5.1 p.481
bearings.system_side: fit_smoreg_essays.py refits a LinearSVR on binary y/n labels (0/1 targets) and searches 12 settings on the same folds.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper figures verified. Table 12 SMO values are E 54.93, ES 57.35, A 55.78, C 55.29, O 62.11, so the 55 to 62 range is rounded. The grid search picks the best of 12 settings on the same folds, so its CV figure is optimistic, as stated. The paper's binary accuracies are not comparable to the system's refit since the features differ (Empath-augmented).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper side holds with rounding (E 54.9 not 55). Page for Table 17 is p.481 not p.480. The system-side code description matches the cited lines. Unverified: the 53 to 58 percent CV figure (no output log was checked) and the claim that these weights were active on 07-03; the script writes mairesse_smoreg.json.candidate, not the active file.

bearings.paper_claim: On EAR, observer-rated Naive Bayes beats baseline for E 73.00 vs 47.78, ES 73.89 vs 51.11 and C 67.67 vs 47.78. No self-report classifier or regressor significantly beats baseline. Mean inter-observer pair r is 0.54 for E, 0.29 for ES and 0.51 for C (18 observers, 31 to 33 pairs).
bearings.paper_location: Table 14 p.476-477; Sec 4.2 p.476; Table 19 and pair r in Sec 5.2 p.482; Sec 8 is p.490-491 (rel says p.492)
bearings.system_side: b5_gold_multitrait_validate.py evaluates predictions separately against the senate_insiders and academic_experts panels; the E and N pass results are system outputs, not checked here.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The EAR design is verified: observers rated audio only, without knowing the participants, in three groups, and the ratings were averaged (EAR description p.464-465). The Senate known-figure reputation point is outside the paper, and the paper never discusses Senate panels. Linking the ES observer agreement to the system's N gate is the verifier's inference.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 14 values, self-report nulls and pair r values verified. Softened: the Sec 8 page cite is wrong (p.490-491), and the paper does not address the system's panel choice. The claim that E and A pass both panels and N passes insiders only is a system result that was not checked.

bearings.paper_claim: Prosody-only RankBoost gives extraversion ranking loss 0.26 (random 0.50), the best single feature set in ranking. Prosody-only Naive Bayes gives 67.56 percent for E, but LIWC alone (68.89) and MRC alone (68.78) are higher. Self-assessed neurotics show low and constant voice intensity (Int-mean, Int-stddev) that observers do not use.
bearings.paper_location: Table 22 p.485; Table 15 p.478 (rel says p.477); Sec 3.3 p.469-470 (Table 11)
bearings.system_side: b5_audio_eval.py defines ES_acoustic as minus the mean of the stability columns (line 97), and a 2026-07-09 note marks the composite as mis-signed.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The 0.26 and 67.56 figures and the self-report intensity result are verified. The strongest-single-feature-set claim holds only for ranking; in classification LIWC and MRC are higher. EAR observers rated audio, so prosody gains are partly shared-channel, as the paper does not test. The sign correction is supported only for self-reported neuroticism, which the rel states.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers verified. Softened: prosody is the strongest single set for extraversion only in ranking (Table 22), not in Naive Bayes classification (Table 15). The system code (line 97) makes low variability ES-positive, which matches the 07-09 note; the paper's self-report result is consistent with that note being wrong.

bearings.paper_claim: In conversation only a high word count and a low mean pitch mark ES in both self and observer reports. Observed ES tracks swearing and anger words but self-assessed ES does not. Self-references and negative-emotion words mark neuroticism in essays, citing Pennebaker and King.
bearings.system_side: emit_affective_n.py keeps the LIWC i + negemo - posemo term only as a convergent anchor (r +.24), not as a component.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper compares essays and student conversation, not political genres, so the link to floor speech is an analogy. The genre-transfer rho values (.050, .161) are not checked here and are not in the paper.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claim verified in Sec 3.3. The anchor role matches the comment at emit_affective_n.py lines 41-43. The rho values and the claim about the LIWC term being dropped from the component were not re-run.

related.why: Ramey et al. apply the pre-trained Mairesse SMOreg to floor speech (text lines 130 and 183-190). Their footnote 4 says observer-trained models; footnote 8 says SMOreg versus M5 made little difference. Their line 191 calls the training sample essay, so the provenance is inconsistent within Ramey.
Review of LIWC and personality language. It shares the LIWC dictionary with this paper but does not supply the essays data, which is Pennebaker and King 1999 (cited, not in this review).
Meta-analysis of 52 LIWC categories against the Big Five that reports small effect sizes. This supports the point about small closed-vocabulary signal; the paper does not cite Mairesse 2007.
Online appendix to expert evaluations of senators. The link to this paper is conceptual (observer or expert ratings); the appendix does not mention Mairesse 2007.
Personalised models for self-reported personality recognition. It does not cite Mairesse 2007, so the link is topical only; the rel labelled it extends, which is not supported.
Cites Mairesse 2007 as reference 179 and calls it the foundation of personality computing with accuracy below 62 percent. Celli discusses threats in general, not Mairesse-specific validity threats.

summary_issues: Paper figures and table cites in the rel summary largely check out against the text. Page cites are off: Table 17 is p.481, Section 8 is p.490-491, Table 15 is p.478.

Unverified: that the active mairesse_smoreg.json holds the RKH refit for all five traits. fit_smoreg_rkh.py writes liwc/rkh_calibrated.json.candidate, which is absent; the essays script writes mairesse_smoreg.json.candidate. The 'replaced trait by trait' history is not in code read here.

Overstated: the claim that big5_traits.py:13-16 describes the model as essays-trained. Those lines describe a pre-trained standardized SMOreg and say nothing about essays; essays wording is only in fit_smoreg_essays.py:4-5, which matches Mairesse's own setup. Ramey is itself inconsistent (fn 4 observer models, line 191 essay sample), so calling this a factual code error is not established.

Wrong: prosody as the strongest single feature set for extraversion holds only in ranking (Table 22). In Table 15 LIWC (68.89) and MRC (68.78) beat prosody (67.56). The summary line that prosody helps extraversion most needs the same qualification.
Unverified: the essays CV range of 53 to 58 percent and the claim that the essays weights were active on 07-03.

Unsupported in the paper: that the distributed observer model was fit on all 96 speakers; that the paper itself warns no cross-corpus test was run (search found no such statement); and that the EAR observer design is the gold standard for the system's N gate.
paul_alignment is unverifiable: paul_entries is empty, so statements about Paul's notes and position have no source here.
Outside this paper, not verified here: held-out r values vs RKH (.510 for E, .350 mean) and the acquaintance-level accuracy label, which come from brain records.
